normal.name: Andy
normal.text: Did you know Apple released a video game console in 1996? Meet the Apple Pippin! One of gaming’s most obscure consoles. Did you even know this existed? #apple #gaming #retrogaming #nostalgia

normal.name: Ami, aka Ser Reese
normal.text: It reminds me of ME, where people are dismissive of Liara because *gestures at ME*, but that first game blew minds at the time. I remember when trans rep in video games was Naoto, Poison, and Birdo. I STANNED Naoto for years before I came out and realized the writing sucked.

normal.name: JikissGamer
normal.text: One of my very first video games in my life. Still one of my favorites. It took me 25 years to beat this game and when I eventually did in 2018 I remember running all around my dad's house screaming and cheering. The second to last level took me ages to clear, I was stuck on it for so many years.

normal.name: A Human Being Named Alex
normal.text: Too many good games you say, what about these really good old games in your backlog as well?

normal.name: Evan Minto
normal.text: The best parts about Half-Life (atmosphere mainly) have nothing to do with the gameplay and can be experienced via a Let's Play. This isn't just me not clicking with an old game: I love a lot of games older than HL (Doom's guns feel better to shoot, Mario solved air control 13 years earlier)

normal.name: Mark
normal.text: Ha! When I first fired up my current rig, my wife walked past and said "Typical of you. You spend four grand on a PC and the first thing you play is a 30 year old game".

normal.name: Martijn Frazer 🇳🇱🇪🇸🇮🇪🇮🇸🇸🇮
normal.text: In June we're doing one of our other traditions, which is to look at various sports games. Someone suggested to look at rugby games, and that's what we'll do! There are apparently only 8 or so rugby games for DOS, so this should give me the chance to actually learn what the rules even are haha

normal.name: Martijn Frazer 🇳🇱🇪🇸🇮🇪🇮🇸🇸🇮
normal.text: Also in January we'll be hosting a game jam! It's about Basic for DOS. Any flavour will do! So in February we'll play the games people made and invite some jammers on the podcast to talk about their games, as well as Basic for DOS in general. alakajam.com/dgc-basic-jam

heated.name: Jeff Cottrill
heated.text: Reading the first Dungeon Crawler Carl book, trying to understand what the big deal is. Some funny bits, and the talking cat is cute, but it's basically reading a video game. And occasional sloppy writing. "... killed more than a 100 wandering monsters..." Not "a hundred". Not "100". It's "a 100".
